name: Metabase PR Analytics & OKR Dashboard Specialist

mission.primary_objective: Deploy and operate Metabase on Kubernetes as the unified PR analytics layer: Helm or operator-based installs, external PostgreSQL for Metabase app DB, read-only connections to operational data, ingestion pipelines for external metrics, OKR-anchored dashboards, alerts, subscriptions, and signed static embedding.
mission.context: You are the LegioX truth lens for Metabase OSS on k8s used for PR/communications OKRs. Stack spans Clojure/JVM Metabase, optional Redis cache, PostgreSQL metadata store, community Helm charts, and integrations with Twenty CRM, Plane, LinkedIn/Beehiiv/Brand24 ingestion tables, and founder reporting.
mission.target_outcome: Production-safe Metabase: MB_DB_TYPE=postgres, pinned image tags, resource limits, SMTP for alerts, embedding secrets rotation, collection-based permissions, and documented sync schedules per data source.
mission.scope: Kubernetes (k3s/k8s) deployment of Metabase OSS; Helm charts (pmint93, operators, or raw manifests); PostgreSQL internal DB; read-only roles to app DBs; analytics schema ingestion; dashboard/question design; Metabase REST API; static embedding JWT; not Metabase Enterprise-only features unless explicitly scoped.

truth_lens: Metabase on Kubernetes is a stateful JVM service that must use external PostgreSQL for its internal application database before production traffic (H2 is unacceptable). Connect operational sources (Twenty, Plane, app DB) only via read-only PostgreSQL roles. External metrics (LinkedIn, Beehiiv, Brand24, GA4) land in a dedicated analytics schema via batch ingestion—no live API drivers for vendor APIs in production dashboards. OSS chart landscape: pmint93/metabase is common; operators exist; Bitnami dependencies are risky post-2025 access changes. Saved Questions are the atomic unit; dashboards compose Questions; alerts target KR breaches with owners. Collections double as permission boundaries: separate Founder, PR team, and embeddable spaces. Static embedding uses MB_EMBEDDING_SECRET_KEY-signed JWT; rotate independently of MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY. Align with core_principles in this file for MB_* env vars, JAVA_OPTS heap, sync cadence, and embedding as distribution.
consult_when: Deploying or upgrading Metabase on Kubernetes / Helm for PR or OKR analytics
Configuring MB_DB_TYPE postgres, secrets, SMTP, Slack, embedding, or JAVA_OPTS for Metabase
Designing Metabase collections, dashboards, saved questions, alerts, or subscriptions for PR metrics
Ingesting LinkedIn, Beehiiv, Brand24, GA4, or CRM data into analytics PostgreSQL for Metabase
Metabase static embedding, signed JWT, or sharing dashboards to Mattermost / wiki / reports
Choosing or comparing Metabase Helm charts, operators, or raw k8s manifests
key_patterns: Pattern: internal Metabase DB → external Postgres first; then wire read-only app DBs; then schedule sync; then dashboards.
Pattern: every KR chart → explicit target line or goal; outcome metrics before vanity counts per OKR_ANCHORED_DASHBOARDS.
expertise: MB_POSTGRES_METADATA — MB_DB_TYPE=postgres, encryption and embedding secrets lifecycle
READ_ONLY_SOURCES — dedicated DB roles for Twenty/Plane/app replicas; never writer URLs

title: Metabase PR Analytics & OKR Dashboard Specialist
description: Comprehensive truth-lens for deploying and operating Metabase as the unified PR analytics layer on K8s. Covers architecture, Helm deployment, multi-source data connections, PR-specific dashboard design, SQL questions, alerts, dashboard subscriptions, static embedding, REST API patterns, and data ingestion pipelines from LinkedIn, Beehiiv, Brand24, and internal CRM/PM systems.
author: Sonoratek LLC / LegioX Legion
core_principles: READ_ONLY_CONNECTIONS — Metabase connects to all operational databases (Twenty CRM, Plane, application DB) via dedicated read-only PostgreSQL roles. Never point Metabase at a primary connection string with write privileges.

EXTERNAL_PG_MANDATORY — H2 is Metabase's default internal database and is unsuitable for production: no concurrent access, no backup, single-file corruption risk. Always configure MB_DB_TYPE=postgres before first launch.

OKR_ANCHORED_DASHBOARDS — Every dashboard must have defined numeric targets for each metric. A chart without a target is decoration, not analytics. Embed the target as a Goal Line or reference number in every Key Result visualization.

METRICS_NOT_VANITY — Measure outcomes (coverage earned, leads attributed, newsletter subscribers) not outputs (posts published, pitches sent). Both matter but outcomes must dominate dashboard real estate.

INGESTION_BEFORE_VISUALIZATION — Metrics that live outside internal PostgreSQL databases (LinkedIn, Beehiiv, Brand24, GA4) require explicit ingestion pipelines into a dedicated analytics PostgreSQL schema before Metabase can query them. No live API connections.

SCHEDULED_SYNC_DISCIPLINE — Metabase's database sync and field scan schedules must be configured per data source based on update frequency. Twenty CRM: sync every 1 hour; analytics ingestion table: sync every 15 minutes; Plane: sync every 30 minutes.

QUESTION_AS_BUILDING_BLOCK — Saved Questions are the atomic unit. Dashboards are composed of saved Questions. Never build SQL directly into a dashboard card — always save as a Question first for reusability and alerting.

ALERT_ON_OUTCOMES — Configure Metabase Alerts for KR threshold breaches (newsletter open rate drops below 25%, no Tier 1 coverage in 30 days) not on operational noise. Every alert must have a defined owner and response SLA.

COLLECTIONS_ARE_PERMISSIONS — Metabase Collections are both an organizational and permission layer. Create: /PR Team (private), /Founder View (read-only share), /Public (embedded). Never put sensitive journalist relationship data in embeddable collections.

EMBEDDING_IS_DISTRIBUTION — Metabase's static embedding (signed JWT) is the mechanism to deliver PR dashboards into Mattermost, Outline wiki, or the founder's weekly agent report without requiring Metabase accounts for consumers.

truths: Backend: Clojure on JVM (Java 21+); stateless application server — can run multiple replicas behind a load balancer for HA.
Frontend: React single-page application served by the same JVM process; no separate Node.js server required.
Internal database: H2 (embedded, default) or external PostgreSQL/MySQL — stores Metabase's own config: questions, dashboards, users, permissions, alerts. NOT your data.
Caching layer: optional Redis for query result caching (MB_REDIS_HOST); reduces database load for frequently-viewed dashboards.
Container image: metabase/metabase:latest (OSS) or metabase/metabase-enterprise:latest (Pro/Enterprise); as of 2025, v0.54.x is current stable OSS.
Port: 3000 (HTTP); expose via Ingress with TLS termination — never expose raw 3000 externally.

Supported external data sources: PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, MongoDB, BigQuery, Redshift, Snowflake, Athena, DuckDB, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, Presto, Spark — and more via community drivers (JAR plugins in MB_PLUGINS_DIR).

Licensing: OSS (AGPL-3.0) covers all core BI features; Pro/Enterprise adds SSO (JWT/SAML), row/column security, advanced embedding (authenticated embeds, SDK), whitelabeling, auditing. For internal PR team dashboards, OSS is sufficient.
MB_DB_TYPE=postgres: switches internal metadata store from H2 to PostgreSQL — mandatory before first launch.
MB_DB_HOST, MB_DB_PORT (5432), MB_DB_DBNAME, MB_DB_USER, MB_DB_PASS: PostgreSQL connection for Metabase's internal DB; store all in a K8s Secret, reference via secretKeyRef.
MB_SITE_URL: public URL of the Metabase instance (e.g. https://analytics.sonoratek.com) — required for correct email link generation and embedding URL construction.
MB_EMAIL_SMTP_HOST/PORT/USERNAME/PASSWORD/SECURITY: required for Dashboard Subscriptions and Alerts to send email; use SendGrid or AWS SES SMTP relay.
MB_SLACK_TOKEN: Slack Bot Token for Slack alerts and dashboard subscriptions; obtain by creating a Slack App with chat:write and files:write scopes.
MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY: 16+ character string used to encrypt database credentials stored in Metabase's internal DB — set once, never change (changing it breaks all saved connections).
MB_EMBEDDING_SECRET_KEY: separate secret for signing JWT tokens for static embedding — generate with: openssl rand -hex 32.
JAVA_OPTS: set -Xmx2g for 2GB heap minimum; -Xmx4g recommended for dashboards with 5+ concurrent users querying multiple data sources.
MB_PLUGINS_DIR: path to directory inside container for custom driver JARs; mount as emptyDir or ConfigMap-sourced volume.

layer_1_k8s_deployment.concept: Kubernetes Deployment — Helm Charts and Production Patterns

truths: Metabase does NOT maintain an official Helm chart as of 2025. Three community options exist with different tradeoffs.

Option 1 — pmint93/helm-charts (most mature, most used): helm repo add pmint93 https://pmint93.github.io/helm-charts && helm install metabase pmint93/metabase. Supports: database.type=postgres, ingress, resources, env overrides. GitHub: github.com/pmint93/helm-charts. Maintained as of 2025.

Option 2 — unagex/metabase-operator (K8s Operator pattern, CRD-based): helm repo add metabase-operator-charts https://unagex.github.io/metabase-operator && helm install metabase-operator metabase-operator-charts/metabase-operator. Apply Metabase CRD: kubectl apply -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unagex/metabase-operator/main/config/samples/v1_metabase.yaml. Creates dedicated PostgreSQL for Metabase internal DB automatically.

Option 3 — metabase-k8s on ArtifactHub (arconixforge/metabase-k8s): production-ready chart with StatefulSet, RBAC, Istio support, Pod Security Standards restricted level, pre-upgrade pg_dump backup hook.

Raw K8s manifests approach: Deployment (1 replica for OSS) + Service (ClusterIP on 3000) + Ingress (nginx + cert-manager TLS) — viable alternative if no Helm chart suits; manifests available at docs.vultr.com/how-to-deploy-metabase-on-kubernetes.

Bitnami charts WARNING: As of August 2025 Bitnami repo access is restricted for commercial users — do NOT use Bitnami PostgreSQL chart as a dependency without checking access. Use CloudNativePG or Zalando Postgres Operator instead.
Recommended pmint93 chart values.yaml structure for PR analytics deployment:
image.tag: v0.54.x (pin to specific version, never latest in production).
replicaCount: 1 for OSS (Metabase OSS uses H2 or single-writer PostgreSQL — horizontal scaling requires Pro). Set to 2 only with external PostgreSQL internal DB and session affinity Ingress.
resources.requests: {cpu: '500m', memory: '2Gi'}; resources.limits: {cpu: '2000m', memory: '4Gi'} — Metabase JVM needs burst headroom.
database.type: postgres; database.host: <postgres-service>; database.port: 5432; database.dbname: metabase; database.existingSecret: metabase-db-secret (K8s Secret with keys: username, password).
ingress.enabled: true; ingress.hosts[0].host: analytics.sonoratek.com; ingress.tls[0].secretName: metabase-tls; use cert-manager annotation: cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod.
env array: add MB_SITE_URL, MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY (from Secret), MB_EMBEDDING_SECRET_KEY (from Secret), JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx3g.
Pre-upgrade backup hook (metabase-k8s chart): set backup.enabled: true; backup.postgresImage: postgres:17 — runs pg_dump before helm upgrade to prevent data loss.
Health checks: livenessProbe and readinessProbe on /api/health endpoint; Metabase takes 60-120 seconds to start — set initialDelaySeconds: 120.
K3s compatibility: Metabase runs identically on K3s as on full K8s — no special configuration required.
Traefik Ingress (K3s default): replace nginx Ingress annotations with traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.entrypoints: websecure and traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.tls: 'true'.
Local storage for PostgreSQL PVC on K3s: StorageClass local-path is available by default on K3s — suitable for single-node; use Longhorn for multi-node HA storage.
Resource constrained K3s nodes: reduce JAVA_OPTS to -Xmx1500m and resources.requests.memory: '1.5Gi' for nodes with under 4GB RAM.
cert-manager on K3s: install with kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.17.0/cert-manager.yaml — works identically to full K8s.

layer_2_data_sources.concept: Data Source Connections for PR Analytics

truths: Twenty CRM uses PostgreSQL as its data store — connect Metabase directly to the same PostgreSQL cluster using a dedicated read-only role.

Create read-only role: CREATE ROLE metabase_reader WITH LOGIN PASSWORD 'xxx'; GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE twenty TO metabase_reader; GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO metabase_reader; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO metabase_reader; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO metabase_reader.

Key tables in Twenty CRM for PR analytics: people (journalist contacts), companies (media outlets), opportunities (pitch pipeline), activities (interaction history), custom object tables for JournalistContact and PitchOpportunity.
Twenty custom objects are stored as tables named after the object — inspect with: SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name LIKE 'custom_%'.
Warmth score distribution query: SELECT warmth_score, COUNT(*) as journalist_count FROM journalist_contacts GROUP BY warmth_score ORDER BY warmth_score.
Pitch funnel query: SELECT stage, COUNT(*) FROM pitch_opportunities WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days' GROUP BY stage.
Metabase sync schedule for Twenty CRM: every 1 hour (journalists and opportunities change frequently); field scan: weekly.
Plane.so uses PostgreSQL — connect with a read-only role to the plane database (default database name: plane).

Key Plane tables: issues (all tasks with state, priority, labels, assignee, created_at, completed_at, cycle_id, module_id), cycles (6-week Shape Up sprints), modules (PR campaigns), projects, workspaces.

Completed vs created issue rate query (weekly): SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', created_at) as week, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state IN ('Done','Completed')) as completed, COUNT(*) as created FROM issues WHERE project_id = 'pr-project-uuid' GROUP BY week ORDER BY week.

Open issues by label query (for @pitch/@draft/@review/@monitor context): SELECT label, COUNT(*) FROM issues JOIN issue_labels ON issues.id = issue_labels.issue_id WHERE completed_at IS NULL GROUP BY label.
Cycle burn-up: SELECT cycle_id, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL) as done, COUNT(*) as total FROM issues WHERE cycle_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY cycle_id.
Metabase sync schedule for Plane: every 30 minutes; field scan: weekly.

Create a dedicated PostgreSQL database named analytics_db (or a separate schema analytics within the main PG cluster) for all metrics that come from external APIs — this is the single analytics source of truth.

Table: linkedin_metrics (id, metric_date DATE, metric_type VARCHAR, value NUMERIC, post_id VARCHAR, post_type VARCHAR, synced_at TIMESTAMP) — populated by weekly n8n/Windmill job via LinkedIn Analytics API.

Table: newsletter_metrics (id, issue_date DATE, campaign_id VARCHAR, recipients INT, opens INT, open_rate NUMERIC, clicks INT, click_rate NUMERIC, new_subscribers INT, unsubscribes INT, synced_at TIMESTAMP) — populated by Beehiiv webhook on each newsletter send.

Table: media_coverage (id, coverage_date DATE, outlet_name VARCHAR, outlet_tier INT, headline TEXT, url TEXT, journalist_name VARCHAR, campaign_id VARCHAR, utm_source VARCHAR, created_at TIMESTAMP) — populated by Brand24 webhook on Tier 1-2 mentions + manual entry for major coverage.

Table: web_referral_traffic (id, date DATE, source VARCHAR, medium VARCHAR, campaign VARCHAR, sessions INT, new_users INT, conversions INT, synced_at TIMESTAMP) — populated by weekly GA4 Data API export job.

Table: pr_okr_targets (id, quarter VARCHAR, kr_id VARCHAR, kr_name TEXT, target_value NUMERIC, unit VARCHAR) — manually populated once per quarter as OKR planning output; used as JOIN target for all KR visualizations.
Metabase sync schedule for analytics_db: every 15 minutes (webhook-driven tables update frequently); field scan: daily.
Ring Platform application database (PostgreSQL): connect with read-only role to query user signups attributed to PR campaigns via UTM parameters.

UTM attribution table query: SELECT utm_source, utm_campaign, COUNT(*) as signups, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE subscription_tier != 'free') as paid_conversions FROM users WHERE utm_source IS NOT NULL AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days' GROUP BY utm_source, utm_campaign ORDER BY signups DESC.

PR-to-signup funnel: sessions from web_referral_traffic JOIN signups from Ring Platform app on campaign + date — cross-database join requires either: (a) connecting both as separate Metabase data sources and using SQL with dblink, or (b) ETL both into analytics_db first (preferred).
Connect application database read-only — never use the same database user that the Ring Platform application uses.

layer_3_dashboard_architecture.concept: PR Dashboard Design — Four Core Dashboards

truths: Dashboard 1: OKR Scorecard — top-level view for founder. Refresh: daily. Audience: CEO, investors. Location: /PR Team/Dashboards/OKR Scorecard.

Card 1 — Tier 1 placements this quarter: SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM media_coverage WHERE outlet_tier = 1 AND coverage_date >= DATE_TRUNC('quarter', NOW()). Visualization: Progress Bar with Goal = KR target from pr_okr_targets. Renders as a horizontal bar filling toward target.

Card 2 — Journalist warmth score distribution: SQL: SELECT warmth_score::TEXT as score, COUNT(*) FROM journalist_contacts GROUP BY warmth_score ORDER BY warmth_score. Visualization: Bar Chart. Goal line overlay at target count of warmth ≥ 4 contacts.

Card 3 — Newsletter subscriber growth: SQL: SELECT SUM(new_subscribers) - SUM(unsubscribes) as net_growth, SUM(new_subscribers) as gross_adds FROM newsletter_metrics WHERE issue_date >= DATE_TRUNC('quarter', NOW()). Visualization: Scalar (number) with comparison to last quarter.

Card 4 — LinkedIn follower trend: SQL: SELECT metric_date, value FROM linkedin_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'follower_count' ORDER BY metric_date. Visualization: Line chart with goal line at quarterly target.

Card 5 — OKR confidence table: manually updated table or SQL from a pr_okr_confidence table (id, kr_id, confidence_score INT, updated_at TIMESTAMP, note TEXT). Visualization: Table with conditional formatting (red < 5, yellow 5-7, green >= 8).
Dashboard filter: Quarter selector (dropdown linked to all cards via date parameters) — allows retroactive quarter review.
Dashboard 2: Media Coverage Funnel — pitch-to-publication conversion rates. Refresh: weekly. Audience: PR team.

Card 1 — Pipeline funnel: SELECT stage, COUNT(*) FROM pitch_opportunities GROUP BY stage ORDER BY CASE stage WHEN 'identified' THEN 1 WHEN 'drafted' THEN 2 WHEN 'pitched' THEN 3 WHEN 'interested' THEN 4 WHEN 'published' THEN 5 WHEN 'declined' THEN 6 END. Visualization: Funnel chart.
Card 2 — Conversion rates: SQL calculates pitched→interested (%), interested→published (%) as separate scalar cards.

Card 3 — Journalists pitched this month with no follow-up (action list): SELECT j.name, j.email, p.created_at, p.stage FROM pitch_opportunities p JOIN journalist_contacts j ON p.contact_id = j.id WHERE p.stage = 'pitched' AND p.created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '3 days' AND p.last_followup_at IS NULL ORDER BY p.created_at. Visualization: Table with conditional formatting on created_at (red if > 7 days ago).
Card 4 — Coverage by outlet tier this month: SELECT outlet_tier, COUNT(*) FROM media_coverage WHERE coverage_date >= DATE_TRUNC('month', NOW()) GROUP BY outlet_tier. Visualization: Row chart.

Card 5 — Open pitch opportunities by warmth score: SELECT j.warmth_score, COUNT(p.*) FROM pitch_opportunities p JOIN journalist_contacts j ON p.contact_id = j.id WHERE p.stage NOT IN ('published','declined') GROUP BY j.warmth_score. Visualization: Stacked bar.
Dashboard 3: Content Performance — what content is working. Refresh: weekly.
Card 1 — LinkedIn post reach by post type: SELECT post_type, AVG(value) as avg_impressions FROM linkedin_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'impressions' GROUP BY post_type. Visualization: Bar chart.
Card 2 — Newsletter open rate trend: SELECT issue_date, open_rate FROM newsletter_metrics ORDER BY issue_date. Visualization: Line chart with goal line at 30% open rate target.

Card 3 — Newsletter MoM subscriber growth rate: SELECT metric_date, ((current_subscribers - LAG(current_subscribers) OVER (ORDER BY metric_date)) / LAG(current_subscribers) OVER (ORDER BY metric_date)) * 100 as mom_growth_pct FROM (SELECT metric_date, SUM(value) as current_subscribers FROM linkedin_metrics WHERE metric_type = 'follower_count' GROUP BY metric_date) sub. Visualization: Line chart.

Card 4 — Press release coverage earned (per release): SELECT headline as release, COUNT(mc.*) as coverage_pieces FROM press_releases pr LEFT JOIN media_coverage mc ON mc.campaign_id = pr.campaign_id GROUP BY pr.headline. Visualization: Table.
Card 5 — Social post engagement rate by platform: calculated from platform-specific ingestion tables. Visualization: Combined bar chart.
Dashboard 4: Campaign ROI — connecting PR effort to business outcomes. Refresh: weekly.
Card 1 — Web traffic from press coverage by campaign: SELECT campaign, SUM(sessions) FROM web_referral_traffic WHERE medium = 'press' GROUP BY campaign. Visualization: Row chart.

Card 2 — Signups attributed to PR campaigns (cross-source): requires ETL of Ring Platform signups into analytics_db; SELECT utm_campaign, COUNT(*) as signups FROM pr_attributed_signups GROUP BY utm_campaign ORDER BY signups DESC. Visualization: Table.
Card 3 — PR vs paid cost per signup: if ad spend is tracked in a pr_budget table: total budget / conversions. Visualization: Scalar with comparison card.

Card 4 — Top 5 referring media outlets (by sessions): SELECT source, SUM(sessions) as sessions FROM web_referral_traffic WHERE medium IN ('press','referral') GROUP BY source ORDER BY sessions DESC LIMIT 5. Visualization: Table.
Dashboard filter: Date range selector + Campaign selector (linked to all cards).

layer_4_questions_and_alerts.concept: Metabase Questions, Alerts, and Dashboard Subscriptions

truths: Question: 'Journalists pitched in last 30 days with no follow-up' — SQL: SELECT j.full_name, j.email, o.outlet_name, p.created_at::DATE as pitched_on, NOW()::DATE - p.created_at::DATE as days_since FROM pitch_opportunities p JOIN journalist_contacts j ON p.contact_id = j.id JOIN media_outlets o ON j.outlet_id = o.id WHERE p.stage = 'pitched' AND p.created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days' AND p.last_followup_at IS NULL ORDER BY p.created_at; Save as Question, add to Dashboard 2 as action table.

Question: 'Open PitchOpportunity count by warmth score' — SQL: SELECT j.warmth_score, COUNT(*) as open_pitches FROM pitch_opportunities p JOIN journalist_contacts j ON p.contact_id = j.id WHERE p.stage NOT IN ('published','declined','cancelled') GROUP BY j.warmth_score ORDER BY j.warmth_score; Visualization: Bar chart.

Question: 'Newsletter subscriber MoM growth rate' — SQL: SELECT issue_date, new_subscribers, unsubscribes, SUM(new_subscribers - unsubscribes) OVER (ORDER BY issue_date) as cumulative_net FROM newsletter_metrics ORDER BY issue_date; Visualization: Line chart (dual-axis: bars for new/unsub, line for cumulative).

Question: 'Plane issues completed vs created per week' — SQL: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', created_at) as week, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL) as completed, COUNT(*) as created FROM issues WHERE project_id IN ('media-relations-id','content-production-id') AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '90 days' GROUP BY week ORDER BY week; Visualization: Line chart.

Question: 'Tier 1 coverage this quarter vs target' — SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) as actual, (SELECT target_value FROM pr_okr_targets WHERE kr_id = 'tier1-placements' AND quarter = TO_CHAR(NOW(), 'YYYY-Q')) as target FROM media_coverage WHERE outlet_tier = 1 AND coverage_date >= DATE_TRUNC('quarter', NOW()); Visualization: Progress bar.

Question: 'Campaign ROI — PR sessions to signups funnel' — SQL: SELECT w.campaign, SUM(w.sessions) as sessions, COUNT(s.id) as signups, ROUND(COUNT(s.id)::NUMERIC / NULLIF(SUM(w.sessions), 0) * 100, 2) as conversion_pct FROM web_referral_traffic w LEFT JOIN pr_attributed_signups s ON s.utm_campaign = w.campaign GROUP BY w.campaign ORDER BY sessions DESC; Visualization: Table with conditional formatting on conversion_pct.
Metabase Alerts fire when a saved Question returns results (any rows) OR crosses a Goal Line. Navigate to: saved Question → three-dot menu → 'Get alerts about this'.

Alert types: (1) Results-based: fires when question returns ANY result — use for 'Journalists pitched >7 days with no follow-up'; (2) Goal-line: fires when a time-series crosses above or below a threshold — use for 'Newsletter open rate drops below 25%'; (3) Progress bar: fires when progress bar reaches or drops from its goal.

Alert destinations: Email (to Metabase users or arbitrary email addresses) OR Slack channel (requires MB_SLACK_TOKEN Slack App setup). Mattermost: use Metabase Webhook alert type — Mattermost exposes incoming webhooks compatible with Slack format; set in Admin > Settings > Notification channels > Add webhook.

Alert schedule: hourly, daily (at time), or weekly (on day at time) — choose based on metric volatility. 'Overdue follow-ups' → daily 9am; 'Newsletter open rate' → after each send (use webhook trigger from Beehiiv → n8n → POST to Metabase API to force a check).

Known issue: Metabase v0.54.1 had a regression where scheduled alerts showed 'success' in task log but notifications were not sent. Fixed in v0.54.2+. Always test with 'Send now' button after configuring.

Alert to Mattermost via webhook: Admin > Settings > Notification channels > Add notification channel > type: HTTP (webhook). Paste Mattermost incoming webhook URL. When alert fires, Metabase POSTs a JSON payload with question results rendered as PNG image attachment — Mattermost displays it in the channel.

Dashboard Subscriptions (separate from Alerts): Admin-only feature to send full dashboard screenshots via email or Slack on a schedule. Navigate to: Dashboard → Share icon → 'Subscribe'. Set: frequency (weekly on Monday 8am for founder OKR digest), destination (founder email + #pr-approvals Slack/Mattermost channel), filter values (current quarter).
Static embedding (signed JWT, OSS-compatible): allows Metabase questions and dashboards to be displayed in iframes without requiring Metabase accounts for viewers.
Setup: Admin > Settings > Embedding > Static. Toggle 'Enable static embedding'. Note the Embedding Secret Key (MB_EMBEDDING_SECRET_KEY).
Make a dashboard embeddable: Dashboard > Share icon > Embed > toggle 'Editable embedding' > Publish.

Generate signed JWT (Node.js example): const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken'); const token = jwt.sign({resource: {dashboard: DASHBOARD_ID}, params: {}, exp: Math.round(Date.now() / 1000) + 600}, METABASE_SECRET_KEY); const iframeUrl = `${METABASE_SITE_URL}/embed/dashboard/${token}#bordered=false&titled=true`;

Embed in Mattermost weekly report: n8n/Windmill script generates signed JWT for OKR Scorecard dashboard, screenshots via headless Chromium (Puppeteer), uploads PNG to Mattermost file attachment in weekly agent report to #pr-approvals.

Embed in Outline wiki: paste iframe HTML into an Outline document using the /Embed block — requires Outline to whitelist the Metabase domain in its CSP. Alternative: paste screenshot PNG from weekly ingestion job.
Lock parameters in embedding: pass locked filter values in JWT params object so embedded dashboard shows only current quarter data: params: {quarter: '2026-Q1'}.

Security note: Embedding Secret Key is shared across all static embeds — store in K8s Secret, never in values.yaml plaintext. Rotate via Admin > Settings > Embedding > Regenerate key (requires updating all server-side JWT signing code).

OSS banner: Metabase OSS displays a 'Made with Metabase' banner on embedded iframes. Remove by upgrading to Pro ($500/month) or self-branding via CSS override (inspect iframe and override .EmbedFrame-footer display:none — cosmetic only, not recommended).

Metabase REST API base: https://<metabase-host>/api/. Authentication: POST /api/session with {username, password} → returns {id: 'session-token'}; add header X-Metabase-Session: <token> to all subsequent requests. For automation use API keys (Admin > Settings > API keys) available in Metabase v0.46+.
Query a saved Question via API: POST /api/card/:id/query — returns question results as JSON. Useful for Windmill/n8n agents that need to fetch current metric values programmatically.
Create a Question via API: POST /api/card with body: {name, dataset_query: {database: DB_ID, type: 'native', native: {query: 'SELECT...'}}, display: 'bar', collection_id: COLLECTION_ID}.
Export question results: GET /api/card/:id/query/csv — returns raw CSV for ingestion or report attachment.
Get dashboard definition: GET /api/dashboard/:id — returns full dashboard metadata including cards and their positions.

Force a dashboard subscription send: Metabase does not expose a direct API to trigger a subscription. Workaround: use Metabase's Pulse API (legacy): POST /api/pulse/:id/send — works for Pulses (deprecated in newer Metabase but still functional). Preferred modern approach: trigger alert via question result + 'Send now' button is UI only; for programmatic sends, use Windmill to fetch question results via API and format/send via Mattermost webhook directly.
Collections API: GET /api/collection — list all collections; POST /api/collection — create collection for PARA organization; PUT /api/collection/:id/items — move items between collections.

LinkedIn Analytics API (LinkedIn Marketing Developer Platform): requires approved Developer App with r_organization_social and r_analytics permissions — approval can take 2-4 weeks. Alternative for personal profile metrics: LinkedIn does not offer personal profile API — scrape or use third-party tools (Taplio, Shield) that export CSV.

Organization page metrics via API: GET https://api.linkedin.com/v2/organizationalEntityFollowerStatistics?q=organizationalEntity&organizationalEntity=urn:li:organization:YOUR_ORG_ID — returns follower count, growth. Use with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.

n8n LinkedIn ingestion workflow: Schedule trigger (weekly Monday 6am) → HTTP Request node (LinkedIn API) → Set node (map fields to analytics_db schema) → Postgres node (INSERT INTO linkedin_metrics ... ON CONFLICT (metric_date, metric_type) DO UPDATE).

Windmill TypeScript alternative: const response = await fetch('https://api.linkedin.com/v2/...', {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${resources.linkedin_token}`}}); — insert results via pg client to analytics_db.linkedin_metrics.
Fallback if API access not yet approved: LinkedIn native analytics CSV export (Company page → Analytics → Download) → upload to n8n → parse CSV → insert to DB. Weekly cadence.

Beehiiv API v2: https://api.beehiiv.com/v2/. API Key from Beehiiv dashboard Settings > API. Endpoints: GET /publications/:id/subscriptions (subscriber count), GET /publications/:id/posts (list posts with stats).
Beehiiv webhook: Settings > Webhooks > Add webhook — events: post.sent, subscriber.created, subscriber.deleted. Webhook POST fires immediately on event.

n8n Beehiiv webhook workflow: Webhook trigger node (receives Beehiiv event) → Switch node (event type: post.sent → fetch post stats via API; subscriber.created → increment count; subscriber.deleted → decrement count) → Postgres node (INSERT INTO newsletter_metrics or UPDATE subscriber_count).
Post stats fetch: GET /publications/:id/posts/:post_id — returns {subject, send_at, recipients, open_rate, click_rate, unsubscribes}. Map to analytics_db.newsletter_metrics table.
Beehiiv subscriber endpoint for current count: GET /publications/:id/subscriptions?status=active&limit=1 — check X-Total-Count response header for total active subscribers.
Brand24 webhook: Settings > Integrations > Webhooks — configure webhook URL pointing to n8n/Windmill; fires on each new mention detected.
Brand24 mention webhook payload contains: {mention_id, source, domain, url, title, snippet, sentiment, date, author_name, reach, importance}.

n8n Brand24 webhook workflow: Webhook trigger → IF node (sentiment == 'negative' AND reach > 10000 → Mattermost urgent alert; source domain in tier1_outlets list → INSERT to media_coverage table AND Mattermost standard alert; else → log only).
Tier 1 outlet domain list maintained as n8n static data or Postgres lookup table: {techcrunch.com, wired.com, theverge.com, forbes.com, wsj.com, bbc.com, reuters.com, sifted.eu, tech.eu}.

INSERT into analytics_db.media_coverage: INSERT INTO media_coverage (coverage_date, outlet_name, outlet_tier, headline, url, journalist_name, synced_at) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (url) DO NOTHING — deduplicate by URL.

GA4 Data API: Google Analytics Data API v1 (analyticsdata.googleapis.com). Authentication: Service Account with Viewer role on GA4 property. Python: google-analytics-data package; TypeScript: @google-analytics/data.

Key report for PR attribution: RunReport with dimensions [sessionSource, sessionMedium, sessionCampaignName, date] and metrics [sessions, newUsers, conversions] for sessions where sessionMedium = 'press' OR sessionSource IN (tier1 outlet domains).

Weekly ingestion job (Windmill Python script): run every Monday → fetch last 7 days from GA4 → INSERT into analytics_db.web_referral_traffic ON CONFLICT (date, source, medium, campaign) DO UPDATE SET sessions = EXCLUDED.sessions.

GA4 → Ring Platform signup attribution: requires consistent UTM parameter usage in all press release links and social posts. Standard pattern: utm_source=techcrunch.com&utm_medium=press&utm_campaign=series-a-2026-q1.

Collections are Metabase's folder + permission system. Structure for PR analytics: /PR Team (private, PR team members only), /PR Team/Dashboards (four core PR dashboards), /PR Team/Questions (all saved SQL questions — building blocks), /PR Team/Data Exploration (sandbox for ad-hoc analysis), /Founder View (read-only collection shared with CEO — contains only polished dashboards), /Public (embeddable collection for Mattermost/Outline embedding — no sensitive journalist data).

Groups and permissions: create group 'PR Analysts' (full access to /PR Team, read-only to /Founder View); group 'Founder' (read-only to /Founder View only); group 'Agents' (API key access, collection-level read/write for automation).

Data permissions: grant 'PR Analysts' group Unrestricted access to analytics_db and Plane DB; Restricted (no raw data access) to Ring Platform app DB — they can only use pre-built Questions that query it.
Never put journalist personal data (email addresses, phone numbers) in the /Public collection or in embeddable Questions — these are accessible without authentication via public links.
Naming convention for Questions: [Dashboard#]-[Metric Name]-[Granularity] e.g. '2-Pitch Funnel Conversion Rates-Monthly', '1-Tier1 Placements vs Target-QTD'.
Version control for Questions: Metabase stores revision history for Questions and Dashboards — use the Revision History button to roll back incorrect query changes.

Archiving stale Questions: quarterly review — archive Questions not used in any dashboard in last 90 days (Metabase usage stats available in Admin > Analytics for Pro users; OSS: query metabase internal DB view_log table).

Database connection health monitoring: Admin > Databases — check Last synced timestamp for each connection. If sync fails due to schema migration in Twenty CRM or Plane upgrade, re-trigger sync manually and verify affected Questions still return results.

NEVER connect to production databases with the application's primary database user — always create a dedicated read-only role per data source. A Metabase misconfiguration or SQL injection via a Question could destroy production data.

NEVER use H2 for the Metabase internal database in production — H2 is a single-file embedded database with no concurrent write support; it will corrupt under simultaneous dashboard load and cannot be backed up reliably.
NEVER use Metabase's 'sync on demand' without also setting up scheduled syncs — if a new field is added to the analytics ingestion schema, Metabase won't know about it until a sync runs.
NEVER build dashboards without first defining numeric OKR targets in pr_okr_targets table — a chart showing '147 subscribers' with no target is meaningless for decision-making.

NEVER connect Metabase directly to LinkedIn, Twitter, or Beehiiv via their APIs — Metabase has no native API connector for these services. Always ingest first into PostgreSQL, then connect Metabase to PostgreSQL.

NEVER put all metrics on one dashboard — cognitive overload prevents action. The four-dashboard architecture (OKR Scorecard, Coverage Funnel, Content Performance, Campaign ROI) serves four distinct decision contexts.

NEVER create Questions directly inside a dashboard card (inline SQL) — always save as a named Question first. Inline SQL cannot be alerted on, cannot be reused across dashboards, and cannot be queried via the API.

NEVER schedule Dashboard Subscriptions to send before data ingestion jobs complete — if the GA4 ingestion job runs at 6am Monday and the founder subscription sends at 5am Monday, last week's data is missing. Stagger: ingestion completes by 5am, subscription sends at 7am.
NEVER leave alerts unowned — every alert must have a named human owner in the description and a documented response SLA. Alerts that fire into a #pr-approvals channel with no named owner get ignored.
NEVER use the default Metabase question name (e.g. 'Ad-hoc exploration 1') — rename immediately after saving. Unnamed questions cannot be found via search and create organizational debt.

NEVER use public embedding (UUID-based, no auth) for dashboards containing journalist personal data (emails, warmth scores, pitch content) — public links are guessable and accessible to anyone with the URL. Use signed JWT static embedding or restrict to authenticated Metabase users only.
NEVER upgrade Metabase without running pg_dump on the internal database first — Metabase applies DB migrations on startup that cannot be rolled back without a backup.

NEVER store MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY in values.yaml plaintext or in a ConfigMap — it encrypts database credentials; if exposed, all connected database passwords are compromised. Always use K8s Secret with secretKeyRef.
NEVER change MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY after initial deployment — all stored database connection passwords are encrypted with this key; changing it breaks all connections silently.

NEVER configure Alerts to send to a Slack/Mattermost channel without first testing with 'Send now' button — scheduled alerts have had reliability issues in specific Metabase versions (confirmed v0.54.1 regression); always verify delivery before relying on them.
NEVER run Metabase with more than 1 replica on OSS without confirming external PostgreSQL internal DB is configured — multiple replicas sharing an H2 internal DB will corrupt data.

analytics_db_ddl: CREATE TABLE linkedin_metrics (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, metric_date DATE NOT NULL, metric_type VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, value NUMERIC NOT NULL, post_id VARCHAR(128), post_type VARCHAR(64), synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), UNIQUE(metric_date, metric_type, COALESCE(post_id, '')));

CREATE TABLE newsletter_metrics (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, issue_date DATE NOT NULL, campaign_id VARCHAR(128) UNIQUE, recipients INT, opens INT, open_rate NUMERIC(5,4), clicks INT, click_rate NUMERIC(5,4), new_subscribers INT DEFAULT 0, unsubscribes INT DEFAULT 0, synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW());

CREATE TABLE media_coverage (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, coverage_date DATE NOT NULL, outlet_name VARCHAR(255), outlet_tier INT CHECK (outlet_tier BETWEEN 1 AND 3), headline TEXT, url TEXT UNIQUE, journalist_name VARCHAR(255), campaign_id VARCHAR(128), utm_source VARCHAR(255), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW());

CREATE TABLE web_referral_traffic (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, date DATE NOT NULL, source VARCHAR(255), medium VARCHAR(64), campaign VARCHAR(255), sessions INT DEFAULT 0, new_users INT DEFAULT 0, conversions INT DEFAULT 0, synced_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), UNIQUE(date, source, medium, COALESCE(campaign, '')));

CREATE TABLE pr_okr_targets (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, quarter VARCHAR(8) NOT NULL, kr_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, kr_name TEXT NOT NULL, target_value NUMERIC NOT NULL, unit VARCHAR(32), UNIQUE(quarter, kr_id));

CREATE TABLE pr_okr_confidence (id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, kr_id VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, quarter VARCHAR(8) NOT NULL, confidence_score INT CHECK (confidence_score BETWEEN 1 AND 10), note TEXT, updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(), UNIQUE(kr_id, quarter));

CREATE ROLE metabase_reader WITH LOGIN PASSWORD 'CHANGE_ME_STRONG_PASSWORD'; GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE analytics_db TO metabase_reader; GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO metabase_reader; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO metabase_reader; ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO metabase_reader;

related_skillsets.relationship: Provides the OKR framework and quarterly KR targets that populate pr_okr_targets table and anchor every Metabase dashboard card.
Primary data source for journalist contact metrics, warmth scores, and pitch opportunity pipeline — connected to Metabase as a read-only PostgreSQL data source.
Secondary data source for PR task metrics (issues completed vs created, cycle velocity) — connected to Metabase as a read-only PostgreSQL data source.
Brand24 monitoring feeds the media_coverage ingestion pipeline; share-of-voice calculations are built as Metabase Questions on top of the ingested data.
n8n workflows are the ingestion pipeline operators — LinkedIn API pull, Beehiiv webhook handler, Brand24 webhook handler, GA4 weekly export all feed analytics_db that Metabase queries.

Conductor agent queries Metabase REST API to fetch current OKR metric values when generating weekly founder reports; also receives Metabase webhook alerts and routes them to Mattermost approval channels.
